title: One Awareness in Every Seat
hookLine: a packed bus home, and the same knowing in every seat
carry: one awareness, shiva, shines in every body
tomorrow: your mind wanders off mid-sit. where exactly did it go?

cards: The last bus home, packed to the doors. A nurse still in scrubs, asleep against the window. Two kids sharing one pair of earbuds.
A man on the phone saying I know, I know, to someone who can't see him nod. Nobody looks at anybody. Each person is a whole world, sealed shut, riding the same bus.

And a question floats up somewhere between stops: is the seeing behind each pair of eyes as private as it feels? The Vijnana Bhairava has a verse with an answer, and it's not the one the bus would suggest.

teach.h: THE GODDESS ASKED; BHAIRAVA GAVE DOORS.
teach.b: Remember how this book began: the Goddess asked Bhairava what he really is, and instead of a description he gave her doors. Here's one, in plain words.

teach.h: KNOWER AND KNOWN, IN EVERY BODY.
teach.b: The awareness of knower and known, someone seeing something, is common to everyone who has a body. What sets the practiced apart, Bhairava says, is attention to it.
They notice the knowing itself; everyone else looks straight through it to the thing that's known. A neighboring verse goes further.

A wanting, a knowing, the awareness of something as ordinary as a clay pot: these don't arise only in me, it says. They arise in others too. Hold that steadily, and a person becomes as wide as everything.
Now the big teaching underneath, named plainly.
In Kashmir Shaivism, the school that treasures this book, Shiva is consciousness itself: one awareness, shining in every being.

It's a cousin of the Upanishads' old claim that the self in you, the atman, is not finally separate from Brahman, the one reality. So the nurse, the kids, the man on the phone aren't similar lamps in separate boxes.
On this teaching, it's one light, in every seat.

teach.h: NAMASTE: A BOW TO THE DIVINE IN YOU.
teach.b: That's why many teachers read the everyday namaste, palms pressed together, as a bow to the divine in the other person.

Notice the turn this run has taken. The breath, the fading sound, the first flicker of a want all happened inside one person. This door opens outward, to the stranger across the aisle who will never learn my name.

how: In Kashmir Shaiva study, verses like this are read slowly with a teacher and sat with in meditation, the attention turned from the thing known to the knowing itself.

o: a book of hymns that praise the Goddess by name
a ritual manual of offerings for Shiva's temples
a tantric book of short practices, doors to awareness

games.q: what does the verse say about awareness? tap the pairs.
p: common to all who have a body
set apart by attention to it
arises in others too, not only in me
a person becomes wide as everything

s: awareness is private, lit only behind your own eyes
the verse says the awareness of knower and known is common to everyone who has a body.
the Vijnana Bhairava says only yogis are truly aware
everyone is aware; what sets the practiced apart is attention to the knowing, which this school calls Shiva.
a verse says wanting and knowing arise in others, not only in me
held steadily, it says, that makes a person as wide as everything.

games.q: your lab partner keeps drifting off in class and it's starting to bug you. which thought fits today's verse?
o: she's lit by the same awareness, Shiva, that's lit in me.
most people sleepwalk through life; only meditators are awake.
awareness is inward work; keep your attention on your own breath.
games.why: the verse says the awareness of knower and known is common to everyone with a body. in Kashmir Shaivism that awareness is Shiva himself; the practiced don't own it, they notice it.

practice: Listen for the farthest sound you can hear: traffic, a fan, a voice through a wall. Somewhere near that sound, someone else is hearing too.
Rest in your own hearing, and let it sink in that the same plain knowing is lit in them right now.

wordCard.voice: The Vijnana Bhairava: a tantric book of doors. Today's door is the one awareness, Shiva himself in this school's teaching, lit in everyone who has a body.

orig.note: Sanskrit vijnana, knowing, consciousness; the first word of the book's title.

carryVoice: For the road: one awareness, Shiva, shines in every body, even on the last bus home. Day sixteen twenty-five.

sources.ref: Vijnana Bhairava, the dharana on the awareness of subject and object (grahya-grahaka) as common to all embodied beings, yogis distinguished by attentiveness to it
Vijnana Bhairava, the neighboring dharana (desire, knowledge and the awareness of a pot arise in others too; one becomes all-pervading)
Kashmir Shaiva teaching that Shiva is consciousness (chit) itself, one awareness in all beings; the namaste reading is a common teachers' reading, labeled as such
